name: Under-eye concealer

lead: Under-eye concealer is a pigmented makeup used to cover dark circles and redness. Men on forums discuss it as a quick way to look more rested.
It works by covering, not treating, and no trial studied it for dark circles.

paras: Pigment in the product blends with skin tone to hide discolouration under the eyes.
No harms are documented in the sources reviewed. Forum posters mention cakey or visible results when the shade or amount is off.

lead: Under-eye concealer is a pigmented cosmetic applied to the skin beneath the eyes to mask dark circles, redness or discolouration. Grokipedia describes concealer as thicker and more pigmented than foundation and intended for small areas.[1]

In looksmaxxing communities it is discussed as a quick, temporary way to brighten the eye area, and some men's forum posts describe how to use it so it does not look like makeup.[2] No clinical trial of concealer for dark circles was found; related research examines what correlates with dark-circle severity.[3]

paras: Concealers come in several formulations aimed at blemishes, scars, redness and under-eye circles.[1] Grokipedia traces camouflage cosmetics to ancient Egypt and Greece and credits Lydia O'Leary with Covermark in 1930, originally marketed for scars and birthmarks.[1] Grokipedia is AI-generated and unverified.
A 2021 study examined correlates of severity of periocular dark circles.[3] A 1988 paper discussed the need for, evaluation of and use of corrective cosmetics.[4]

Forum posts include a guide titled around using concealer on dark circles without looking like makeup, and threads about how men can buy and hide concealer purchases.[2][5] One poster describes applying concealer the day before and sleeping in it, and says it looked cakey up close when a relative noticed.[6]
No studies found on concealer as a treatment. Related studies examine dark-circle severity and corrective cosmetics generally.[3][4]

lore.intro: Men on looksmaxxing forums discuss concealer as an accessible first cosmetic step, with discussion of discretion and shade matching.[2][5]

claims.claim: Concealer can hide dark circles without looking like makeup.
Concealer is a hard-to-obtain item for men because of social stigma.

timeline.event: Lydia O'Leary develops Covermark, per Grokipedia.[1]
